title: Mini pita pizzas
skill: Halving or doubling a recipe for the family

notes.text: Use two sheet pans, one on each rack, and swap them halfway through.

move.title: Measure it, then make it fit
move.body: Each pita pizza gets a measured amount of sauce and cheese, so every one comes out the same. This is the unit's mastery week: you'll work out how much you need for your family, halving or doubling the recipe, then make it on your own.

why.title: Level the cup
why.body: A heaped cup of cheese can hold half again as much as a level one. Fill the cup loosely, then sweep a table knife across the top. That's one cup.

why.title: Wet in a wet cup
why.body: Liquids go in a clear measuring cup with a spout, read at eye level. Dry ingredients go in a cup you can level off. A spoonful of sauce is measured with a measuring spoon, level.

why.title: Halving and doubling
why.body: This recipe makes 4 pizzas. For 8, double every amount: 2 times each one. For 2, halve every amount. Write the new numbers down before you start, so you don't have to work them out with sauce on your hands.

why.title: A thin layer of sauce
why.body: Too much sauce soaks the pita and the cheese slides off. Two tablespoons, spread to just inside the edge, is enough.

why.title: Soft vegetables, small knife
why.body: Mushrooms and a pepper are soft enough for a paring knife. Lay them flat side down and use the claw grip, the same as week 1's tomatoes.

wrong.fix: Use less sauce, and bake the pitas plain for 3 minutes first next time.

wrong.sign: The cheese browned before it melted
wrong.fix: Move the rack down one level and check a few minutes earlier.

wrong.sign: There wasn't enough cheese for the last pizza
wrong.fix: Measure each one level, and check your doubled numbers before you start.
Check 2 minutes early. Pitas are thin and brown fast.

quiz.q: How do you level a cup of shredded cheese?
choices: Fill it loosely and sweep a table knife across the top
quiz.explain: A heaped cup holds much more.

quiz.q: The recipe makes 4. How much sauce for 8?
quiz.explain: Twice as many pizzas, twice the sauce.

quiz.q: How do you read a liquid measuring cup?
quiz.explain: From above, it looks fuller than it is.

substitutions.note: Use gluten-free bread slices, toasted first so they stay crisp.

steps.text: Read the recipe. If you're cooking for more or fewer than 4, write down each amount halved or doubled.
steps.tip: 8 people: double everything. 2 people: halve everything.

steps.text: Move a rack to the middle while the oven is cold. Heat the oven to 425°F.
Lay a damp paper towel under the cutting board. Rinse the pepper and wipe the mushrooms clean with a damp paper towel.
steps.tip: Mushrooms soak up water, so wipe them instead of rinsing.

steps.text: Cut the pepper in half with the bridge grip. Pull out the seeds, lay it flat side down, and slice thin strips.
steps.look: Thin strips, close to the same width.

steps.text: Lay each mushroom on its flat side. Hold it with the claw grip and slice it thin.
steps.look: Thin slices you can almost see through at the edges.

steps.text: Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you.
Lay the pitas on the sheet pan. Brush the tops lightly with olive oil.
Measure 2 level tablespoons of sauce onto each pita. Spread it to just inside the edge.
steps.tip: Use the back of the spoon to spread it in circles.

steps.text: Measure ¼ cup of cheese for each pita, leveled with the table knife, and sprinkle it on.
steps.look: An even layer, sauce peeking through in spots.

steps.text: Add the pepper and mushrooms. Sprinkle a pinch of oregano over each.
steps.tip: Spread them out so every bite gets some.

steps.text: Mitts on. Slide the pan into the oven and bake until the cheese bubbles.
steps.look: Cheese melted and bubbling, edges golden.

steps.text: Mitts on. Pull the rack out, lift out the pan, and set it on the stovetop. Turn off the oven.
steps.tip: Tell anyone nearby the pan is hot.

steps.text: Let the pizzas cool for 2 minutes before eating.
steps.tip: Melted cheese is hotter than it looks.
